why: A (universes 0; IsCompatible is a definition = the Corollary 8.4 formula itself): (a) Cor. 8.4 for the induced connection P(dY(v)) of a slice submanifold N ⊆ V, for fields differentiable at q; (b) for a Mathlib connection on an abstract Riemannian manifold (any model), 'the Cor. 8.4 formula holds for fields differentiable at the point' ↔ Mathlib's IsMetricCompatible. B: on an abstract ℝⁿ-manifold, a smooth connection compatible in MILNOR's sense (parallel fields, defined via ∃ D obeying axioms (a)-(c), have constant inner products) satisfies the Cor. 8.4 formula for smooth Y, Y'. B is exactly 'Milnor-compatible ⇒ IsCompatible (on smooth fields)'; A ⇒ B fails genuinely because that implication is Lemma 8.3 on an abstract manifold (parallel orthonormal frames along a curve with velocity X_p, i.e. abstract Lemmas 8.1/8.2), which the project does not have: it takes the Cor. 8.4 formula as the definition of compatibility (Connection.lean: Milnor's definition 'cannot be stated without parallel transport'). B ⇒ A is vacuous: both clauses re-proved outright (product rule + ⟨Pu,w⟩ = ⟨u,w⟩; Mathlib's isMetricCompatible_iff). B cannot be specialized to N ⊆ V: the induced metric/connection are not packaged as a Mathlib RiemannianBundle/CovariantDerivative on N.
